precepts.text: Aaron took Elisheba, Amminadab's daughter and Nahshon's sister, to wife; priests and kings intermarried, which is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins, and why Eleazar the high priest had a mother of Judah.
precepts.point: Hezron begat Ram, Ram begat Amminadab, Amminadab begat Nahshon the prince of the children of Judah, and from Nahshon come Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

precepts.text: Amram took him Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses; the scripture names the parents of Moses.
precepts.point: A man of the house of Levi took to wife a daughter of Levi. These are Amram and Jochebed, the father and mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
Exodus 2 says only that “there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.” Exodus 6 gives their names: “And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.”

The man of the house of Levi is Amram, and the daughter of Levi is Jochebed. They are the father and mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

precepts.text: Aaron married Elisheba and she bore him children, establishing Amminadab in the lineage, because the prophet comes from among the brethren, meaning from a man.
precepts.point: Peter is quoting Moses, and every scripture in the New Testament is quoted from the Old, so there is no such thing as reading only the New Testament and skipping precept upon precept.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The prophet comes from among the brethren, from a man, so follow the men. “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Here Amminadab and Naashon are established in the lineage of Israel in the days of Moses. Those same names show up in the generation of Christ, which is how we know he was raised up from among his brethren.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
Anything we are going through, the answers are in the Bible. Not in the Quran: you never heard of a New International Quran; they don’t tamper with that Quran because there is no truth in there, no history, no prophecies, nothing that tells you who you are or who the people of the past are. No other book on the earth is more powerful than the Bible. It gives history, present time and future prophecies all through it, and that is why they are scared for us to read our book: the solutions are in this book, because we are the people of this book.

“According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness.” God’s divine power has given it to the Israelites. Not some things, not 99 percent: all things that pertain to this life you are living right now. Everything is in this book. Depressed, it is in here; anxiety, it is in here; suicidal thoughts, he tells you how to get around it. Mourning for somebody who passed, or your faith is low, he has it in here: how to build your faith, exalt you and comfort you through his words. That is what Romans 15:4 says: through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
We are broken people; God says we are broken. “Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”: that is the broken spirit, the mental distress and physical distress we are going through. You want something, you are looking for something, but if you are in the world you are not going to find it. You are looking for change, you go to politics and voting, and it is not there. You go to all these nonprofit organizations, Jesse Jackson, Al Sharpton and all these people: none of these things are going to help you. You have to come back to your Bible to get the help you need. Looking for change where it is not makes your mind sick, distressed and aggravated; it messes with your mind.

“But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.”

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”: we are going to keep revolting more and more against our Father. “The whole head is sick”: all our leaders out there in so-called displaced America, all the leaders we are supposed to look up to, are messed up. None of them have solutions for our problems. None of them come into the ghettos to help our people or build our people back, and even the people who have money don’t come back to their communities to build them up.

“And the whole heart faint”: your mind is weary, distressed, broken. That is why we have to go back to this Bible and rebuild our spirits. We have to get our minds right, Israel, and trust back in the Lord and in our record book that God gave us.

precepts.why: What tribe was Moses from? “These are the families of Levi according to their generations. And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses.” Moses was a Levite, and his father’s name was Amram. Note it down for the lineage.

note.label: Book Of Our Fathers: Who's Who Part 2

precepts.why: “And Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas: these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.” Phinehas was the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Many names within our nation denote black appearance; Acts 13:2 is not the only one. “Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas”.

The scholars give the meaning of Phinehas: it comes from an Egyptian name, from the word the Egyptians used for their southern neighbours, which came to mean the black, or the Nubian; another work renders it the bronze-coloured one; and Brown-Driver-Briggs gives it plainly as the negro. That is not something we made up; the scholars know it while many of us do not.

Phinehas was Aaron’s grandson, so the Levites were black.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
“And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name Jehovah was I not known to them.” That is some heavy stuff right there. He said he appeared unto Abraham, Isaac and Jacob by the name of God Almighty. You read that and say, oh, that is the heavenly Father. It is the Father, but not the Father that you are thinking of.

That is why, when they said teach us to pray, Christ said pray like this: Our Father which art in heaven. The Father he was talking about was not himself but his Father. There is a Godhead in heaven. Our little black minds can't comprehend it, but yes, there is a Godhead; there is a government in the heavens. We have been reading about the 24 elders and all that; you have angels; there is a government up there. You don't do whatever the hell you want up there.

points: These are that Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt; these are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: You should not be ignorant: “I have also heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.” He remembers his covenant with us.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.” He would redeem us “with a stretched out arm, and with great judgments”: he had great judgments on Egypt. “Ye shall know that I am the Lord your God”, Israel, your God, and he would bring us into the land sworn to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and give it to us “for an heritage.”

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

points: “But they hearkened not unto Moses.” We didn’t listen, like today. This is spiritual Egypt we are living in right now all over again, and we are not listening even today to our Lord and Saviour, not listening to the Bible, not changing. Our people love evil, we love wickedness, we love entertainment; we don’t love God like we say we do. Them not listening to Moses was them not listening to the Heavenly Father, and them not listening to us is like them not listening to the Heavenly Father, because we are the messengers he is sending in these last days to wake them up, redeem them from the evil they have been in, and help them become a new person in Christ, with a new spirit and a new mind. Our people are crazy: we find every excuse to do evil.

“For anguish of spirit”: they had a low spirit, a broken spirit. Egypt broke their spirit, and that is what is happening today. A lot of people in this truth have broken spirits, and they run easily back out into the world because they find it safe there: safe in the hand of the enemy, the oppressor, following the heathen, first and foremost Esau, and after that the rest of the heathen, the Moabites, the Ishmaelites. They feel safe following them instead of coming back, following the Lord and this Bible, and coming back to who they are as Israelites. They get comfortable.

Anguish is severe mental or physical pain. That is PTSD: what we had then when we came out of Egypt, and what we have here in America. Our minds are gone, broken and fragile, and we haven’t noticed it yet; we have a mental problem and a physical problem we haven’t dealt with. That is why we deal with our problems through this Bible. “And for cruel bondage.”
